---
title: "Definitions, Bound Inputs, Points, and Optimization"
---

::: {.callout-warning}
## CONVERGING Parameter System concept

The independent definition, Plan-binding, parameter-space, sweep-result, and
parameterized-diagram surface has an integrated implementation baseline but is
not Human-accepted. The [central evidence status](../contracts/index.qmd#implementation-evidence-status)
limits execution claims. Accepted unit,
physical-model, numerical-algorithm, and objective meanings are not reopened.
:::

## A number, a named input, and a search variable are different things

A literal such as `110 * u.fF` is already a complete physical value. It should
remain literal when no external operation needs to vary it. Naming that value
as an input does not make it an optimization variable, and choosing a search
variable does not make the computed quantity a circuit input.

The Parameter System keeps seven layers distinct:

| Layer | Meaning |
|---|---|
| baseline value | the definition's immutable default physical value |
| `ParameterSpec` | scalar unit and dimensional validation |
| `ParameterRef` | one input identity: definitions-collection ID plus local ID |
| physical binding | one or more registered component fields that consume the ref |
| `ParameterSet` | one immutable operation-time point |
| `ParameterSpace` | an ordered Cartesian grid or explicit list of points |
| `OptimizationVariable` | one scalar ref plus request-local finite bounds and transform |

The output selected by an objective is a typed quantity, not a `ParameterRef`.
`root_hint` remains a numerical branch locator, not a parameter value, target,
bound, or Gate.

## Definitions are independent; physical fields assign them to a Plan

`ParameterDefinitions(id="readout_design")` owns a namespace. Its
`parameter(id=..., baseline=..., spec=...)` method returns an immutable ref but
does not register that ref with a Plan. The ref becomes an input of a specific
Plan only when a real component field consumes it and that component is added
to the Plan or one of its owned subsystems.

The ref's identity key is exactly the definitions-collection ID plus local ID.
Its schema and canonical baseline must agree wherever that key is reused; a
conflict is rejected rather than becoming another same-named parameter.
The collection ID is a stable logical namespace, not a Notebook caption or
Python variable name. Recreating the same compatible collection/local-ID key is
intentional; a conflicting definition is rejected when a Plan or operation
consumes it. Unrelated designs should not reuse a key casually, and no mutable
global registry is implied.

```text
definition -> ParameterRef -> component physical field -> registered Plan
                                      |
                                      +-> visible Plan-specific consumer evidence
```

Merely constructing a definition, putting a ref in a `ParameterSet`, or using
the same Python object in a Notebook creates no Plan binding. A Plan captures
only its consumed definition-and-binding closure. An unused definition added
later therefore cannot change that Plan snapshot.

One ref may feed several physical fields or several Plans. Those Plans inspect
their own consumers independently. Conversely, equal values held by different
refs remain separate inputs. Literals never acquire refs automatically, and
there is no mutable global current value.

## Reusable components publish a boundary, not their private children

A primitive's `parameter(field_name)` returns its exact original bound ref,
including a mapped field's original input ref, and preserves that identity
across clone/add. Literal fields raise `KeyError` rather than creating refs.
Transmission-line length and whole RLGC inputs follow the same rule.

A Library factory accepts compatible literals or refs through its declared
input arguments. Inside the factory, native fields consume those values.
`CompositePlan.expose_parameter(id=..., parameter=...)` publishes the original
bound ref; the resulting component's `parameter("capacitance")` lookup returns
that same public ref without exposing a private child path.

This boundary can represent deliberate fan-out or an accepted scalar
`AffineMap`. It cannot turn one shared ref into several independent variables,
infer a parameter from a literal, or accept arbitrary Python callback
expressions.

## A point fills values; a space orders points

A `ParameterSet` supplies one point. Values omitted for consumed refs use the
captured Plan baseline. Unknown, unconsumed, or dimensionally incompatible refs
are rejected rather than ignored.

`ParameterSpace.grid(axes=..., fixed=...)` forms a Cartesian product. Axis
order is author order; fixed refs and axis refs must be disjoint.
`ParameterSpace.points(...)` instead preserves an explicit ordered list,
including duplicate positions. Incoming arrays and containers are copied and
frozen, so later mutation cannot rewrite request identity.

An operation with a space returns a `ParameterSweepResult`. Every point stores
its complete effective `ParameterSet`, success state, typed Result or failure,
and exact batch/point identity. Exact selection may use a partial
`ParameterSet` as filters: supplied refs must match, while omitted refs are
wildcards. This differs deliberately from operation-time baseline filling.

Collection is also read-only. A typed `QuantitySelector` gathers only a
quantity the request already computed, preserving units, axes, source indices,
duplicates, and a failure mask. One-axis grids can be shown as curves and
two-axis grids as labeled sample-cell heatmaps after other axes are fixed.
Empty selections stay empty, repeated values keep separate sample positions,
and incomplete or listed samples remain indexed points rather than being
silently reshaped, averaged, or interpolated. A quantity absent because its
point failed numerically is masked with that failure; one not requested by the
Spec is rejected without execution.

## Optimization uses the same binding boundary

`OptimizationVariable` adds finite bounds and an existing transform to one
scalar ref. Bounds are not inferred from a parameter-space grid. An
Optimization request may take a `ParameterSet` for non-active fixed inputs;
overlap with active variables is rejected, and omitted non-active inputs use
their sealed baseline.

Every candidate and the winner record a complete effective `ParameterSet`.
The winner can therefore be re-evaluated or rendered explicitly without
changing the Plan baseline. A `ParameterSpace` is not an implicit batch of
optimizations, and a low cost does not create scientific or Human acceptance.

## Structured RLGC values have a bounded support scope

`RLGCParameterSpec` describes one complete fixed-basis R/L/G/C value. Its
conductor labels, reference conductor, matrix shapes, dimensions, and source
provenance remain explicit. Matrix rows and columns are not sweep axes, and
`n_sections` remains authored component structure.

This candidate supports compatible complete RLGC values for declared Direct,
HB, and applicable operator calculations. It does not support continuous
whole-matrix optimization, implicit interpolation, or tracking one baseline
root across changing RLGC matrices. That is the current support boundary, not
a claim that another mathematical method is impossible. Scalar sweeps and
root tracking at a fixed baseline RLGC value remain separate supported uses.

## Diagrams show one selected physical point

A parameterized schematic takes one `ParameterSet`, never a space. It derives
native values, compiler expansion, labels, and audit evidence from that exact
point. The Plan identity does not change, while expanded and numerical
identities may. The audit distinguishes baseline from selected values and binds
`parameters_sha256` for the complete effective point after baseline filling;
it does not certify a View, solver Result, or optimization.
